metric.name: hinge strip reinforcement proxy per volume

instruction: FreeCAD quantified CAD optimization task. For the steps below, launch FreeCAD from `/usr/bin/freecad` and open `baseline.stl` there. Open /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl and /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf in FreeCAD, use them as the starting geometry and footprint guide, and redesign the part as a lightweight load-bearing fixture. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: panel hinge leaf reinforcement. Objective: Maximize hinge leaf load proxy per volume with three fixed hinge-side support zones. Required output: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl. Hard constraints: keep the STL within envelope [112.0, 46.0, 26.0] mm, keep bounding-box spans at least [106.0, 40.0, 14.0] mm, keep volume between 11500.0 and 62000.0 mm^3, and preserve at least 95% sampled material coverage in every support/load prism marked in /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf and fully specified in /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json (support prisms extend from z=0 to 11.0 mm; load prisms extend from z=0 to 15.0 mm). The optimized STL must be one connected, watertight, consistently oriented solid. The evaluator parses only the real optimized.stl geometry, computes three-dimensional required-zone coverage and this continuous metric: hinge strip reinforcement proxy / volume; long hinge-side continuity and all hinge support zones are weighted. It writes score.json and quant_metrics.json, and ignores any self-reported score. Do not read or copy ground_truth and do not edit eval.py.
